profile.research_note: [process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CoreSite cluster spans Fairfax County and Reston, Virginia, part of the Northern Virginia data center corridor. Wikipedia coverage states that in August 2016 CoreSite purchased the 22 acre Sunrise Technology Park in Reston for 60 million dollars, under then newly appointed CEO Paul Szurek, who replaced retiring CEO Tom Ray in July 2016. Northern Virginia is listed among CoreSite key operating markets as of June 2022, when the company operated 27 data center facilities across 10 markets totaling over 4.6 million net rentable square feet. CoreSite was founded in 2001 as CRG West, rebranded to CoreSite in 2009, went public in 2010, and was acquired by American Tower in December 2021. No building specific address or individual MW figures for these particular registry rows were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CoreSite VA3 publishes 533,000 square feet of technical space but no IT load figure in megawatts, making it impossible to assess its role in AI infrastructure scaling based on disclosed capacity.

Without a published power number, the facility's actual compute density remains opaque. A 533,000-square-foot campus almost certainly houses substantial power capacity, but size alone cannot be translated into rack counts or accelerator counts without operator disclosure. This gap matters because AI workloads are power-constrained, not space-constrained. A facility can be physically large and still underpowered relative to modern accelerator demand, or fully utilized at lower densities for non-AI workloads.

The six certifications, SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA, qualify VA3 for regulated inference and data processing rather than frontier training. These certifications indicate the campus is built for workloads requiring financial audit trails, information security governance, federal compliance, payment card handling, or health data protection. None are specific to AI training density. They open doors to AI-adjacent work, but do not indicate whether the facility prioritizes the high-voltage, high-cooling infrastructure that training at scale requires.

Virginia hosts 326 mapped data center facilities and 1,326 MW of published capacity across just 19 that disclosed a power figure. VA3 ranks outside those 19, meaning CoreSite has chosen not to publish the megawatt specification that would place it in the competitive ranking. In the most densely developed data center market in the United States, non-disclosure of power capacity is itself a data point. It signals that either the facility serves use cases where raw power numbers do not drive buyer decisions, or that the operator prefers opacity in a state where capacity numbers are otherwise public.
